newsitem.title: USA: Cuba's rights record worsened in 1996, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's rights record worsened in 1996, U.S. says.

text.p: The human rights record of communist-ruled Cuba worsened last year with a crackdown on a pro-democracy umbrella group and many other alleged abuses of power, the United States said on Thursday.

"The authorities continued routinely to harass, threaten, arbitrarily arrrest, detain, imprison, defame, and physically attack human rights advocates and members of independent professional associations," the State Department said in its annual worldwide survey of human rights.

"The government's human rights record worsened in 1996," the report said, citing the crackdown against the pro-democracy umbrella group Concilio Cubano, the shooting down on Feb. 24 of two small U.S. civilian airplanes in international airspace and increased reports of deaths due to excessive use of force by police.

The State Department also cited further curbs on the distribution of foreign publications, antagonism to any foreign government criticism of human rights practices, restrictions on foreign contacts with human rights activists and expulsions of visiting foreign journalists.
"The government denied human rights advocates due process and subjected them to unfair trials," the report said.
"Political prisoners were offered the choice of exile or continued imprisonment. Prison conditions remained harsh."
